newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Serb minister rejects tribunal warrants.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb minister rejects tribunal warrants.

text.p: The Bosnian Serb interior minister rejects the authority of the U.N. war crimes tribunal and will ignore its arrest warrants, a U.N. official said on Friday.

The United Nations police commissioner for Bosnia, Peter Fitzgerald, met Bosnian Serb Interior Minister Dragan Kijac on Thursday and discussed whether Kijac had indicted war criminals on his police force, as many have charged.
U.N. spokesman Alexander Ivanko said Kijac denied having any war criminals on his payroll, but also rejected the tribunal's legitimacy.

"He did say he does not recognise the tribunal warrants as evidence that people in his force are war criminals," Ivanko said. "He also said he will not arrest anybody or transfer anybody to the Hague."
The Dayton peace agreement signed last year obligates all parties in Bosnia to arrest and surrender indicted war criminals to the Hague for trial by the U.N. tribunal.
Bosnian Serbs and Croats and neighbouring Serbia and Croatia, which also signed the agreement, have refused to hand over those indicted, many of whom live openly on their soil.
As a result only seven of 75 of those indicted are in custody.
NATO, which has had as many as 55,000 combat troops in Bosnia as part of a peacekeeping force, refuses to launch a "manhunt" but says it will make arrests if troops happen to encounter the suspects.
